name: Do I need waterproofing under bathroom tile in California homes?

mainEntity.name: Is waterproofing necessary under shower and bathroom tile, and what happens if it is done poorly?
mainEntity.text: Is waterproofing necessary under shower and bathroom tile, and what happens if it is done poorly?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waterproofing is one of the most important parts of a bathroom remodel because tile alone does not stop water intrusion. In wet zones, the substrate and membrane system matter as much as the visible finish. If waterproofing is skipped or done poorly, water can seep into framing, flooring, and adjacent rooms, creating hidden damage that is expensive to repair later. Homeowners should ask what waterproofing system will be used, where it will be applied, and whether the contractor has a standard detail for shower pans, niches, corners, and seams. Good waterproofing is not a luxury feature; it is a durability requirement. Cutting corners here can make an otherwise beautiful bathroom fail early.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, proper waterproofing is essential in wet areas such as showers and tub surrounds. Tile and grout are not waterproof by themselves. Poor waterproofing can lead to leaks, mold, subfloor rot, cracked tile, and expensive repairs behind finished surfaces.
